In Public Sector & Government, cybersecurity & zero-trust covers architecture-level security programs: zero-trust network and workload design, identity modernization, threat intelligence and managed detection, cloud posture management, ai-specific security for models and agents, cyber resilience, and the compliance machinery (soc 2, iso 27001, pci dss, dora) that regulated industries must evidence. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: zero-trust architecture & implementation, threat intelligence & managed soc, identity & access modernization — delivered on Achala Sentinel and Achala Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Aging systems with hardening debt meet rising state-grade threats; accreditation cycles slow every change.
Benefits, tax, health and licensing systems never joined; citizens re-submit the same facts to every agency. Fraud and error hide in the seams.
Permits, claims and case files are paper-shaped; processing times measured in months erode trust and increase cost per case.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 7 services from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower — Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation, Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC, Identity & Access Modernization, Cloud Security & Posture Management as the usual core — sequenced through the Achala Method with sector controls: Accessibility (Section 508 / EN 301 549 / WCAG) obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Never trust, always verify — zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Detection that keeps pace — intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
Identity as the perimeter — workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Secure at the control plane — posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
identity-centric access across agencies and third parties (state-grade threat surface reduced with evidence)
CBOM and migration for decade-retention data (harvest exposure closed early)
